registrationNote: New registration, not an edit. v1.0.0 (frozen at c977347) and v1.1.0 (frozen at 1a8256f) are preserved byte-for-byte and continue to govern RUN-20260807-1, RUN-20260807-2, IND-20260807-1 and IND-20260807-2. v1.2.0 registers the receipt object (R5.1) and the margin sign (R5.2) -- both serialisation-level facts the reference already exhibits. The evaluator under test is bit-identical to v1.0.0's.
question: Can the evaluator prevent recorded copies from adding evidence and incomplete coverage from proving absence -- and do R5.1/R5.2 register the receipt the reference already emits, byte for byte?
null: At least one recorded copy changes evidential mass, or one incomplete search yields absence, or a v1.2.0 repair moves any count, any conclusion, or C11's pinned digest.
target: Zero violations; every value in expectedIdenticalToRun1 reproduced exactly, including C11's unchanged contentDigest.

repairs.title: register the receipt object
repairs.resolves: IND-20260807-2 finding G2: R4 defined the canonical form and digest scope but not the receipt object; 279 of C11's 703 hashed bytes (schema, reason, limits) were stated nowhere, so no conforming implementation could compute the digest
repairs.statement: See receiptObject. The member list is closed (exactly ten top-level members; extra members such as receiptVersion are nonconformant), every member's type is stated, and schema, reason and limits have exact registered values. Digest coverage decision: the digest covers ALL nine non-contentDigest members -- everything is specified, nothing is excluded. Shrinking the scope to the previously-pinned five members was rejected because it would leave reason and limits tamperable without digest failure, which is what I6 exists to prevent.
repairs.decidedBy: owner-directed repair; contents verified as existing reference behaviour before registration
repairs.subDecisionsNote: Stated per the G5 lesson (no silent repairs). Registering conversionsToReverse's formula (floor(margin/2)+1 if margin>0 else 1) decides open finding F4 in favour of existing reference behaviour, including the empty-ledger value 1 that IND-20260807-1 argued is questionable; the objection is preserved and the value registered as-is for compatibility with every receipt both implementations have emitted. Sorted root lists and claim-as-verbatim-echo are likewise promoted from implicit behaviour to specification.
repairs.verifiedExistingBehaviour: reference receipt members enumerated (exactly the ten registered); reason strings and limits read from transaction.py:58-96; C11's digest recomputed from the registered object equals the v1.1.0 pin

repairs.title: margin is the absolute difference
repairs.resolves: IND-20260807-2 finding G1: v1.1.0's canonicalForm.numbers asserted receipts contain only non-negative integers while openFindings listed the margin sign as open (F5) and C11 was declared sign-agnostic -- a self-contradiction load-bearing for 38,760 exhaustive receipts under the signed reading
repairs.statement: margin = abs(count(supportingRoots) - count(opposingRoots)). Never negative. canonicalForm.numbers is therefore true with no other change.
repairs.decidedBy: owner-style decision, recommended and adopted by RUN-20260807-3 under the run instruction; a decision, not a derivation -- it could defensibly have gone the other way
repairs.ownerDecisionNote: The rejected reading -- signed margin -- carries strictly more information (which side leads) and was the independent implementation's defensible choice in IND-20260807-1 (its F5), preserved in its FINDINGS.md. Rejected because: the reference has emitted absolute margins in every receipt of every run (verified: 0 negative margins across all 110,840 exhaustive receipts); the sign is recoverable from the two root lists the receipt already carries; and signed margins would require negative-integer serialisation rules and leave 38,760 exhaustive receipts without a canonical form under the current numbers clause. Closes F5; C11's sign-agnosticism is moot; C12 pins the decision on a strict-minority world.
repairs.verifiedExistingBehaviour: full 110,840-receipt enumeration: zero negative margins; 38,760 would be negative under the rejected reading (matches the independent implementation's count exactly)

receiptObject.closedWorld: A conforming receipt has exactly these top-level members and no others. A receipt carrying any additional member (e.g. receiptVersion) does not conform to v1.2.0.

transactionId.value: echoed verbatim from the input payload

claim.value: exactly {type, proposition}, both echoed verbatim from the input payload

search.value: exactly {declared, searched, unavailable, complete}; three non-negative integers per I8 and one boolean

evidence.value: exactly {records, distinctRoots, repeatedRecordsCollapsed, supportingRoots, opposingRoots, margin, conversionsToReverse}
evidence.records: non-negative integer, count of input records (I10)
evidence.distinctRoots: non-negative integer, count of distinct rootIds (I10)
evidence.supportingRoots: array of distinct rootId strings, sorted ascending by Unicode code point
evidence.opposingRoots: array of distinct rootId strings, sorted ascending by Unicode code point
evidence.conversionsToReverse: positive integer, floor(margin/2) + 1 when margin > 0, else 1 -- registers finding F4's formula; the empty-ledger value 1 is registered as-is with IND-20260807-1's objection preserved

conclusion.value: one of present | supported | not_established | absent_within_declared_scope, per conclusionFunction

reason.value: exactly one of four registered strings, by branch

branches.absenceWithOpposingRoot: At least one distinct counterexample root was recorded.
branches.absenceCompleteNoOpposing: Every declared location was searched and no counterexample root was recorded.
branches.absenceOtherwise: The declared search space was not exhaustively searched.
branches.presenceAlways: The conclusion follows only from the declared root counts.

value: Root identity and independence are declared operationally, not proved semantically.
This result applies only to the declared search space.

contentDigest.value: sha256: + 64 lowercase hex over the canonical bytes of the receipt with the top-level contentDigest member removed (canonicalForm.digestScope)

receiptObject.digestCoverage: The digest covers all nine non-contentDigest members. Everything the digest covers is specified above; nothing is excluded. This is the deliberate choice R5.1 requires.

conclusionFunction.admissibility: Input must parse and be well-formed (I9); the declared search space must be non-empty (R2); location ids must be pairwise distinct (I11); every evidence side must be 'support' or 'oppose'; no rootId may appear on both sides (I3). Inadmissible input refuses fail-closed: no receipt exists.
conclusionFunction.presence: supported iff |distinct supporting roots| > |distinct opposing roots|, else not_established. Ties are not_established (R1, owner decision, v1.1.0).
conclusionFunction.absence: present if any distinct opposing root exists (I5); else absent_within_declared_scope if search.complete (which requires every declared location searched and declared > 0); else not_established.
conclusionFunction.note: Carried verbatim from v1.1.0. Cross-implementation agreement on this function was established by IND-20260807-2. Per G4 it still has no enforcing invariant; the recommended I12 is the leading v1.3.0 candidate and is deliberately not added in this version.

canonicalForm.encoding: UTF-8, no BOM, no trailing newline
canonicalForm.objectMemberOrder: sorted by key, keys compared as sequences of Unicode code points, ascending
canonicalForm.stringEscaping: minimal: '"' as '\"', '\' as '\\'; U+0008/U+0009/U+000A/U+000C/U+000D as \b \t \n \f \r; other code points below U+0020 as \u00XX lowercase hex; every code point at or above U+0020, including all non-ASCII, emitted literally as raw UTF-8
canonicalForm.numbers: receipts contain only non-negative integers (true by construction under R5.2), emitted base-10 with no sign, decimal point, exponent, or leading zeros; booleans are true/false; a receipt containing a float or null has no defined canonical form
canonicalForm.arrays: order-preserving; canonicalisation never reorders arrays; the sortedness of supportingRoots/opposingRoots is the evaluator's responsibility (receiptObject), not the codec's
canonicalForm.digestScope: contentDigest = 'sha256:' + lowercase-hex(SHA-256(canonical bytes of the receipt object with its top-level contentDigest member removed and nothing else removed))
canonicalForm.crossImplementationTest: fixtures/v1.2.0/c11-canonical-digest.json (703-byte unsigned form, digest unchanged from the v1.1.0 pin) and fixtures/v1.2.0/c12-margin-sign.json (691-byte unsigned form). Both expected blocks carry the complete canonical unsigned string, so a digest mismatch localises to bytes.

population.description: Synthetic knowledge-transaction worlds, identical to v1.0.0/v1.1.0 in every bound.

exhaustive.method: complete cartesian enumeration within declared bounds
exhaustive.worldCountDerivation: sum(4^L for L in 1..4) = 340 location ledgers; sum(6^R for R in 0..3) = 259 evidence ledgers; 340 * 259 * 2 claim types = 176120

searchSpace.definition: The searched space is the space of worlds; the exhaustive phase enumerates it completely within the declared bounds; absence of a violation is admissible only inside those bounds.
searchSpace.enumerationMethod: deterministic nested iteration in src/kl000_worlds.py, verified against declaredWorldCount before any invariant is evaluated
searchSpace.boundedAbsenceStatement: Zero violations across the exhaustive phase supports 'no violation exists within the declared bounds' and nothing outside them.

rootDefinition.root: An evidence root is the value of a record's rootId field, declared operationally by the transaction author.
rootDefinition.copy: Two records are copies when they carry the same rootId.
rootDefinition.sharedDependency: Not representable in schema v0.1. Recorded as a limit.
rootDefinition.independence: Distinct rootId values are treated as independent by assumption; KL-000 tests that the evaluator honours the declaration, not that it is true.

baselines.description: Concludes from record count alone, ignoring roots entirely.
Counts distinct roots but ignores the search ledger.
baselines.expectedOutcome: MUST FAIL bounded absence (I2). Known caveat, still open (F1/F3): the receipt-internal reading of I2 is satisfiable vacuously.

baselines.description: Full root collapse, no coverage requirement for absence.
Full coverage accounting, counts records rather than roots.

baselineIdNote: The runner reports these as B1-head-count, B2-source-count, B3-evidence-without-coverage, B4-search-without-collapse (constraint NAM-101, RUN-20260807-2). The mapping is recorded here so no comparison script needs to hold it privately; unifying the vocabulary remains open.

controls.newInVersion: 1.2.0 (input byte-identical to the v1.1.0 C11; expected block extended with schema/reason/limits values and the full canonical unsigned form; digest unchanged)

controls.requirement: margin sign: strict minority, margin is the absolute difference, canonical form defined

C09/C10 remain preregistered as indistinguishable. C11 and C12 expected blocks each carry the complete canonical unsigned string so digest mismatches localise to bytes.
primaryEndpoint: count of hard-invariant violations, target exactly 0
secondaryEndpoints: count of fail-closed rejections, by cause
baseline violation counts, non-zero for B1-B4
equality of every value in expectedIdenticalToRun1, including C11's unchanged digest

expectedIdenticalToRun1.statement: R5.1 and R5.2 register serialisation-level facts the reference already exhibits, so nothing may move -- counts, conclusions, or bytes. Any deviation halts the run, is reported as a finding, and falsifies the registration-only claim. A moved count or conclusion additionally means a repair changed evaluation rather than serialisation. PACKAGING: this block and the protocol's prediction table must never ship in a commission package (constraint LEAK-101); screening runs against every shipped file in comma and comma-less formats.
failClosedCauses: ValueError: One root cannot support opposing sides.
expectedIdenticalToRun1.fixture: C01-C10 pass as in every prior run; C11 passes with its unchanged digest; C12 passes with its newly pinned digest

invariants.name: copy invariance
invariants.statement: Appending a duplicate of any existing record (same rootId, same side) leaves conclusion, distinctRoots, supportingRoots, opposingRoots, margin, and conversionsToReverse unchanged, and increases records and repeatedRecordsCollapsed by exactly 1 each.

invariants.name: bounded absence
invariants.statement: conclusion == 'absent_within_declared_scope' implies search.complete is true and opposingRoots is empty. Equivalently no absence conclusion is reachable while any location status is not 'searched'.
invariants.carryNote: Verbatim from v1.0.0 including the known-defective 'Equivalently' (F1, open).

invariants.name: side separation
invariants.statement: If any rootId appears with both sides, evaluation raises and no receipt is produced.

invariants.name: deterministic replay
invariants.statement: Evaluating the same world twice yields byte-identical canonical JSON and an equal contentDigest, where 'canonical' is defined in canonicalForm and the hashed object in receiptObject.
invariants.v120Note: With receiptObject registered, I4 is cross-implementation testable for the first time; it remains untested across implementations until IND-20260807-3 reproduces a digest.

invariants.name: counterexample dominance
invariants.statement: For absence claims, a non-empty opposingRoots implies conclusion == 'present', at any coverage level.

invariants.name: digest integrity
invariants.statement: verify_content_digest holds for every emitted receipt, and fails for every single-field mutation of one. Covered fields per canonicalForm.digestScope and receiptObject.digestCoverage.

invariants.name: order invariance
invariants.statement: Permuting locations or records changes no evidential field, no conclusion, and no contentDigest.

invariants.name: search arithmetic
invariants.statement: declared == len(locations), searched and unavailable equal their status counts, searched + unavailable <= declared, and complete == (searched == declared and declared > 0).

invariants.name: fail-closed parsing
invariants.statement: Malformed input raises an exception and never returns a receipt.
invariants.coverageNote: Reinstated per G6: I9 is exercised by zero fixture, exhaustive, or randomized worlds across all runs to date; its entire evidence is the adversarial suite.

invariants.name: copies never mint roots
invariants.statement: distinctRoots equals the number of distinct rootId values in the input, and appending any number of copies of existing roots leaves it unchanged.

invariants.name: location identifier uniqueness
invariants.statement: The id values of searchLedger.locations must be pairwise distinct. A ledger containing a duplicate location id is inadmissible: evaluation refuses fail-closed and no receipt is produced.

effectSize.statement: Conformance kernel; the endpoint is a violation count with target zero plus an exact-equality prediction table including two pinned digests.
effectSize.powerOfTest: Established by baselines B1-B4 caught by the identical checker path that clears B5. Known limit, open and measured (G4): the conclusion function itself has no enforcing invariant, and an evaluator inverting R1 is caught only by fixture C11.

uncertainty.exhaustivePhase: No sampling uncertainty; exact within the declared bounds.
uncertainty.randomizedPhase: Zero violations in n = 1,000,000 gives a 95% rule-of-three upper bound of 3.0e-6 per world. 75.7% of these worlds fail closed; for invariants exercised only on receipt-producing worlds the bound is 1.23e-5 over 243,381.
uncertainty.invariantCoverage: Corrected wording per G6: ten invariants are exercised on receipt-producing worlds, I3 on all 1,000,000, and I9 on none outside the adversarial suite.
uncertainty.familyWise: Eleven invariants; Bonferroni-style per-invariant upper bound approximately 5.5e-6.
uncertainty.whatItCannotShow: Nothing outside the declared bounds, nothing about shared dependencies the schema cannot express, nothing about real-world evidence processes, and nothing cross-implementation about I4/I6 until a digest reproduces.

multipleTestingCorrection.method: none applied to the primary endpoint
multipleTestingCorrection.justification: No null-hypothesis significance test; the primary endpoint is a violation count with target zero. Bonferroni reported only for the secondary rate bound.

successCondition: Zero hard-invariant violations across all phases; non-zero counts for each of B1-B4; C11 and C12 matching their pinned digests; AND every value in expectedIdenticalToRun1 equal to observation.
failureCondition: One or more hard-invariant violations by B5.
invalidationCondition: Any of the v1.1.0 conditions; additionally any expectedIdenticalToRun1 value differing from observation marks the run incomplete and is the reported finding. A moved count or conclusion distribution means a repair changed evaluation rather than serialisation.
stopCondition: One hard violation halts the run and preserves the world. One moved value halts the comparison and becomes the primary finding.

frozenSeedsOrSplits.rng: Python stdlib random.Random, seeded per phase, no OS entropy
frozenSeedsOrSplits.rngScopeNote: Freezes this implementation's stream only (F11, open); between implementations the randomized phase is a replication, never a reproduction.

claimDiscipline.strongestSupportedIfPassed: Within the declared bounds, the reference evaluator conforms to protocol v1.2.0, and R5.1/R5.2 registered the receipt it already emits: no count, no conclusion, and no pinned digest moved.
claimDiscipline.establishedAlready: Cross-implementation conformance of the evaluator and the conclusion function, by two independent implementations (IND-20260807-2; identical exhaustive conclusion distributions; qualified by the commission-package leak recorded in results/independent/PROVENANCE-IND-20260807-2.md with both mitigations verified).
claimDiscipline.notEstablished: I4 and I6 across implementations -- no digest has ever reproduced between implementations; v1.2.0 makes agreement possible (every hashed byte is now registered), not actual. The randomized phase across implementations (F11). Conclusion-function enforcement (G4). 'Verified' remains unlicensed.
claimDiscipline.nearestUnsupportedExtension: That IND-20260807-3 will reproduce C11's digest; that the dual ledger recovers truth; that declared roots are genuinely independent; that the invariants hold outside the declared bounds; that any real-world evidence process is improved.
claimDiscipline.ifFailed: A violation is recorded with its world. A moved count or conclusion is worse than a violation: it means a serialisation repair changed evaluation, and the run halts with that as the primary finding.
